title: Accounting Agents research corpus
mission: A public, read-only research corpus that helps people and agents find, understand, and reuse the information needed to build accounting agents.
coverage_note: Combined US research integration 2026-09-17.3: 1,097 records and 200 named questions. It preserves the qualified nongovernmental US nonprofit contribution and restriction package, adds bounded US operating-transaction foundations, a bounded US management-accounting package, and the AA-I127 ERP evidence-boundaries package, and retains the existing 96 subsector profiles, 5,952 applicability screenings and 1,012 individual industry exception reviews. Named answers remain partial or evidence gaps; no whole question family, subsector or detailed industry is assessed sufficient. Existing international material is retained without substituting it for US authority.
review_note: The 2026-09-17.3 edition preserves the prior construction, nonprofit, operating-transaction and management-accounting evidence boundaries and adds the accepted AA-I127 source-to-ledger and ERP evidence-boundaries package. The package uses original-source locators, a synthetic read-only Oracle ERP journal-header fixture, explicit role and framework limits, scoped assessments, and unresolved publisher rights; it does not establish live Oracle tenant completeness, end-to-end deployment evidence, current consolidated Codification review, professional sign-off, operating effectiveness, empirical agent performance or rights clearance. The outgoing 2026-09-17.2 release and prior snapshots remain immutable. Applicability, accounting adequacy, source currency, professional review, empirical support and reuse rights remain independent. The 31-issue backlog remains open; publishing this batch is not acceptance of every ticket.
rights_note: Project-created factual metadata is CC0 1.0. Original editorial content is CC BY 4.0. Software is MIT. External source content is not redistributed or licensed by this project; access is not permission for training or reuse.
coverage_priorities: Reverify inherited source URLs, editions, effective dates, supersession, and evidence classifications; keep release-specific checks current.
Add jurisdiction-specific accounting, audit, tax, payroll, and public-sector authorities beyond the present US, European and selected other coverage.
Deepen real transaction-level and ledger evidence, finance-specific CDC/deletion behavior, ERP completeness and reconciliation examples; documented contracts remain untested here.
Add independent empirical deployment studies, incident and failure reports, and reproducible accounting workflow evidence beyond controlled questions and synthetic datasets.
Resolve dataset-specific and upstream permissions, including TabFormer and the FiFAR/BAF interaction; keep unknown rights unknown.

Deepen construction coverage with current consolidated GAAP review, state-specific tax and public-works rules, contract and job-cost datasets, ERP lineage and professional validation; continue other industry guidance including nonprofit and government implementation.
